task.name: Context assembly integration for prior-run knowledge
task.story_text:
## What

TheForge can include relevant prior-run summaries as advisory context items in future runs, selected from the deterministic knowledge index, admitted only on an admissibility verdict, and scored by relevance.

## Why

The compounding payoff happens when future agents receive the right prior lessons before planning, developing, or reviewing. This story closes the Layer 3 feedback loop at the context-assembly boundary while preserving the trust rule that LLM-authored summaries advise agents but do not drive coordinator decisions.

This is the **consumer** side. #1866 produces the admissibility verdict; this story decides what to do with it and makes the decision inspectable. Because injection cannot include anything without a verdict to consult, the safety layer is a structural precondition rather than an operator promise.

## Acceptance criteria

- Prior-run summaries can appear in assembled context as advisory, droppable context items.
- Injection is controlled by a configuration key (`knowledge.prior_run_context`) that is disabled by default; when disabled, no prior summary reaches any prompt.
- Only summaries carrying an admissible verdict are eligible for inclusion. A summary with an inadmissible verdict, or with no verdict at all, is never included.
- Selection uses deterministic relevance signals such as file overlap, story/domain match, recency, and indexed patterns, and respects the reduced rank carried by a down-ranked verdict.
- Context inclusion is budget-aware: low-relevance prior knowledge is dropped before required context.
- The context manifest records which prior summaries were included, which were dropped, and why — including the admissibility verdict and reason for anything excluded on admissibility grounds.
- An operator can distinguish "no relevant prior knowledge exists" from "prior knowledge exists but was excluded as inadmissible or stale."
- LLM-authored summary prose does not affect routing decisions, budget enforcement, gates, refusal verdicts, or coordinator control flow.
- A run with no relevant summaries proceeds normally with no context-assembly failure.
- Tests cover relevant-summary inclusion, irrelevant-summary exclusion, inadmissible-verdict exclusion, missing-verdict exclusion, disabled-by-default behavior, budget pressure behavior, manifest visibility, and the no-summary path.

## Example

Manifest entries a run should be able to produce:

```yaml
prior_run_context:
  enabled: true
  included:
    - run_id: 4f2a91c              # relevance 0.81, verdict admissible
      reason: file_overlap(sprint/runner.py), domain_match
  dropped:
    - run_id: 9c11e0a
      reason: budget_pressure          # relevant, but required context won
    - run_id: 71bd334
      reason: inadmissible(cited_source_deleted)
    - run_id: 0ae5f92
      reason: inadmissible(no_verdict)
  note: 2 summaries matched but were excluded on admissibility
```

That last line is what lets an operator tell "nothing was known" apart from "something was known and withheld."

## References

- #787
- Depends on #1866.
- ADR-0002 clause 5 (what LLM summaries may and may not influence)
- `docs/plans/knowledge-capture.md`

handoff.summary: Implemented the consumer side of Layer 3 knowledge feedback. Added theforge.task.prior_run_selector, which loads .forge/knowledge/index.yaml (failing closed to no-candidates on a missing, unreadable, or non-v2 index), interprets each entry's persisted admissibility verdict via knowledge_admissibility.interpret_persisted_verdict(), and scores candidates from deterministic index fields only — changed_files vs the assembly file_list, domain/story/story_shape/learned_patterns tokens vs story text, generated_at recency — with a reduced-rank penalty charged against subject-matter score alone. Scoring separates primary signals (file/dir overlap, domain, story, pattern) from boosts (work type, recency) so a boost can never qualify an entry on its own. Summary prose is rendered from the artifact only after eligibility is settled, and is bounded. Added theforge.task.prior_run_manifest for the audit payload (extracted to keep both modules under the 500-line hard convention; the selector decides what an agent may read, the manifest renders what an operator can later see). Wired both into ContextAssembler behind config.knowledge.prior_run_context (default False for direct construction), adding candidates as advisory required=False ContextItems of kind prior_run_summary with drop_reason budget_pressure, leaving non-prior advisory drops on the existing 'budget exceeded' string. ContextPack gained a defaulted prior_run_context payload, serialized per phase by coordinator/audit.py. Per ADR-0002 clause 5 and the plan reviewer's P1, injection is restricted to plan/dev/review and refused for preflight at the selector.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1: prior-run relevance is now decided before admissibility in select_prior_runs. Previously every inadmissible indexed entry was excluded on admissibility grounds and counted toward the manifest note's 'N summaries matched but were excluded on admissibility', so an index holding only an inadmissible summary about unrelated code falsely told the operator that relevant knowledge had been withheld — defeating the exact AC that an operator must be able to distinguish 'no relevant prior knowledge exists' from 'prior knowledge existed but was withheld'. Entries with no primary relevance signal now exclude as not_relevant with admissibility_excluded=False regardless of verdict, so only knowledge this story could actually have used reaches the admissibility bar and the note's counts. Admissibility remains an absolute bar on inclusion — a test asserts relevant inadmissible and verdict-less summaries are still refused after the reorder. Found and fixed the same category error one line lower: candidates exceeding the selection cap were also labelled not_relevant despite having matched; they now report below_selection_cap(N) and the note reads 'N lower-ranked matches not offered'. No other behavior changed: rendering still happens only after eligibility, so prose still cannot create relevance.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 adds prior summaries to ContextAssembler advisory items whenever the config is enabled, without limiting phases. ContextAssembler is called for preflight at src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py:359, and build_preflight_prompt injects ContextPack.content at src/theforge/task/plan_prompts.py:30. Preflight produces sufficiency, complexity, likely-files, and refusal verdicts that drive coordinator behavior. ADR-0002 clause 5 permits summary influence only on plan, dev, and review prompts, so this data flow violates the trust-boundary acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: Explicitly restrict prior-run summary content to plan, dev, and review phases, keeping it out of preflight, and add a test proving an enabled configuration cannot inject prior summary prose into a preflight prompt.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 says to construct ContextItem values with item_type=advisory, but ContextItem in src/theforge/task/context_assembler.py has no item_type field; that field belongs to ContextManifestEntry and is currently derived from required during manifest construction.
  Suggestion: Keep required=False on ContextItem and derive item_type='advisory' when creating ContextManifestEntry, or explicitly include a compatible ContextItem schema change in the plan.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (the word 'stale' is not a machine verdict reason) is retired by the plan's mitigation — machine reasons verbatim, consumer-side stale/not_relevant — but the manifest's note wording must not conflate the two, since the AC explicitly asks the operator to tell 'inadmissible' from 'stale'.
  Suggestion: Emit separate counts in the note (e.g. 'N excluded on admissibility, M excluded as low-relevance/stale') rather than one blended sentence.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 says prior-run items get drop_reason budget_pressure, but the existing dropped_manifest builder (context_assembler.py:185-198) hardcodes drop_reason='budget exceeded' for every dropped advisory item.
  Suggestion: Branch on item.kind == 'prior_run_summary' when constructing the dropped manifest entry, or carry a per-item drop reason on ContextItem; keep the existing string for non-prior items so test_context_assembler/test_generate_audit_log assertions on 'budget exceeded' keep passing.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] There is no existing loader for .forge/knowledge/index.yaml — knowledge_index.py only exposes KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_PATH and rebuild_knowledge_index(); the selector will have to yaml.safe_load and defend the schema itself (schema_version 2, entries list).
  Suggestion: Have the selector treat unreadable/malformed index or non-v2 schema_version as 'no candidates' (fail closed, no exception), consistent with Risk 3's per-item fail-closed mitigation.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
